title: Why Do Knuckles Pop When You Crack Them?
short_title: Why Your Knuckles Pop (Is It Bad?)
description: Why do knuckles pop when you crack them, and is it bad for you? Here is the simple science of joints and bubbles.

scenes.text: Why do your knuckles pop when you crack them?
Your joints sit in a slippery liquid, inside a small sealed bag.
When you pull the joint, the space inside grows and the pressure drops, like pulling the plunger of a syringe.
A gas bubble suddenly forms in the liquid. That is the pop you hear.
You cannot crack the same knuckle again right away, because the bubble needs about twenty minutes to dissolve.
Studies have not found that it causes arthritis. But if it hurts or swells, see a doctor.
